newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SPRING/WHITE WHEAT - MOST BIDS LOWER.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SPRING/WHITE WHEAT - MOST BIDS LOWER.

text.p: Dark northern spring wheat and soft white wheat bids were mostly lower on Tuesday in line with small losses on the Minneapolis Grain Exchange, dealers said.
"We had a bearish (USDA) report but we got support from higher CBOT corn and soybeans," a Minneapolis grain merchandiser said.

On Tuesday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture forecast all 1997 spring wheat production at 585 million bushels, up from its previous estimate of 569 million. Durum wheat production was pegged at 90 million bushels, versus a previous estimate of 81 million.
Sales were slow in the Minnesota markets because harvest is just beginning and farmers are still holding on to their grain, one dealer said.

One merchandiser in Montana said the winter wheat, spring wheat and barley in his area looked excellent and winter wheat yields will probably average 35 bushels per acre versus as normal yields of of 28 to 31 bushels per acre.
